title: Louisiana Leads the Nation in REDI Sites
excerpt: Louisiana now leads the nation with eight sites on the REDI Sites platform, backed by a $50 million expansion of the state's FastSites Program.

featuredImage.alt: Steel frame of an industrial building under construction at sunrise

contentHtml:
Louisiana has strengthened its economic competitiveness by maintaining 125 active Certified Sites and leading the nation with eight sites on the REDI Sites platform. The state is updating its certified site portfolio with current infrastructure and cost information, while the Legislature has appropriated an additional $50 million to the FastSites Program.

Recent major projects, including Aclara's $277 million rare earth separation facility and Faith Technologies' $80.5 million manufacturing investment, demonstrate how site readiness accelerates business location decisions in Louisiana.

title: Our REDI Site Pipeline Is Growing
excerpt: Norfolk Southern has expanded its REDI Sites portfolio to 24 development-ready locations across its 22-state rail network.

featuredImage.alt: Steel frame of an industrial building under construction at sunrise

contentHtml:
Norfolk Southern has expanded its REDI Sites portfolio to 24 locations across its 22-state network, with new designations spanning the Midwest and Southeast. These REDI Sites are development-ready industrial locations validated through a national standard created with the Site Selectors Guild that assesses infrastructure, feasibility, ownership, and workforce readiness.

The program helps companies make rapid location decisions while enabling communities to better compete for investment and job creation opportunities.

title: Round Four REDI Sites Designations Bring New States into the Program
excerpt: The Site Selectors Guild's fourth round of REDI Sites designations recognizes 17 properties and introduces the program to five new states.

featuredImage.alt: Steel frame of an industrial building under construction at sunrise

contentHtml:
The Site Selectors Guild announced its fourth round of REDI Sites designations, recognizing 17 industrial properties that meet investment readiness standards. This round is significant because it introduces the program to five new states — Michigan, Mississippi, New Mexico, Ohio, and Oklahoma — while also showcasing one site's advancement from Bronze to Silver certification status.

The REDI Sites program provides communities with a standardized, consultant-informed approach to evaluating industrial site readiness, strengthening their competitive positioning in site selection decisions.

title: Certified Sites: Site Certification Programs Try to Meet Their Moment
excerpt: Site Selection Magazine examines how certification programs like REDI Sites help communities market pre-qualified, investment-ready properties.

featuredImage.alt: Steel frame of an industrial building under construction at sunrise

contentHtml:
Site Selection Magazine examines how site certification programs have become essential tools in competitive business recruitment, helping communities market pre-qualified properties with documented infrastructure and entitlements. The piece traces the evolution of these programs and specifically references the Site Selectors Guild's REDI Sites program, established in June 2024, noting its rapid growth to 75 enrolled sites.

The authors note that while certifications reduce risk for investors, they remain an imperfect tool — companies still need to pair certified-site status with their own independent due diligence.
